findings.title: Per-resource DB fallback allows DB/cache-fill DoS on denied resources
findings.body: When the cached permission map exists but does not contain the requested resource, Check unconditionally calls getIdentityPermissions (line 139), and getUserPermissions now always queries the DB because its own cache check was removed. The denial cache is keyed by resource name and parent, so it only helps repeat checks of the same resource; an attacker can vary dashboard/folder UIDs to force one permission DB query and one new denial-cache entry per request. Anonymous users are especially exposed: an empty anonymous permission map is cached, so every unique denied resource misses the denial cache and hits the permission store. This creates a cache-penetration DoS and unbounded local/remote cache growth (the in-proc cache has a 10m cleanup interval), even though the permission cache already told us the user has no matching permission.

findings.title: Denial cache key is not scoped by identity type and uses ambiguous concatenation
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key from namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent only. The identity type is missing, but anonymous and renderer identities both use UID "0" (e.g. anonymous:0 and render:0), so a denial cached for a renderer on an action/resource will also deny an anonymous user checking the same action/resource, even if anonymous has permission (and vice versa). The fields are also concatenated with unescaped '_' separators, so UIDs containing underscores can make different (name, parent) pairs produce the same key. Use the full subject/identity type in the key and length-prefix or hash the fields.

findings.title: DB fallback still relies on stale folder-tree cache for newly created folders
findings.body: The new fallback requeries only permissions and then calls checkPermission again at line 146. For dashboards, checkPermission calls checkInheritedPermissions -> buildFolderTree, which first returns the cached folder tree. If the dashboard is in a folder that was just created and is not yet in that tree, the fresh permission map cannot resolve the folder's ancestors, so the check still returns false even though the user has permission on an ancestor folder. The result is then written to the denial cache, potentially extending the false denial beyond the folder cache TTL. To actually fix newly created folders/dashboards, the fallback needs to bypass or refresh the folder cache as well. Existing tests prepopulate folderCache, so they do not cover this.

findings.title: Denial-cache test uses a deny value in permCache and cannot detect a regression
findings.body: The test comments that it is allowing access to prove the denial cache is checked, but it populates permCache with map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats that as a denial, so the test would still pass if the denial-cache short-circuit were removed; the fallback DB store also has no permissions for dash1. Set the value to true (or use a store that errors/counts calls) so the test fails when the denial cache is not consulted, and add coverage that Check writes a denial-cache entry after a fresh DB denial.
